differences.point: Britannica describes escheat as lands failing to a lord within his manor, while Wikipedia defines it as transfer to the government or crown.
differences.quote_britannica: ESCHEAT, in law, signifies any lands or tenparts that cafinally fail to a Lord within his manor.
differences.quote_wikipedia: Escheat / ɪ s ˈ tʃ iː t / (from Latin excidere ' fall away ') is a common law doctrine that transfers the real property of a person who has died without heirs to the government, or in the United Kingdom, crown.

differences.point: Britannica mentions escheat as one of the consequences of tenure, whereas Wikipedia explains it as ensuring property is not left in limbo.
differences.quote_britannica: It is one of the confeugeures of tenure in divary
differences.quote_wikipedia: It serves to ensure that property is not left in "limbo" without recognized ownership.
